review_candidates.title: Preconstruction & Project Controls Lead
review_candidates.description: Preconstruction & Project Controls Lead Full-Time | Remote | Philippines US Residential Remodeling & Construction Compensation: 15–$22 USD/hour, depending on experience; exceptional candidates up to $25/hour Bonus and profit-sharing opportunities available for extraordinary candidates READ FIRST — NON-NEGOTIABLE EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENT This position requires substantial hands-on experience estimating and controlling costs for US-based residential remodeling, additions, and custom homes. Do not apply if you do not have significant direct experience with US residential projects. Experience primarily in commercial construction, government projects, infrastructure, non-US residential construction, drafting, virtual assistance, or quantity takeoffs does not satisfy this requirement. Applicants who do not clearly demonstrate substantial US residential experience in their application will not be considered. Role Overview We are a growing US residential construction company seeking an exceptional Preconstruction & Project Controls Lead to take ownership of the financial and planning side of our projects from preconstruction through execution. This is a hands-on senior position with significant long-term growth potential. Initially, you will personally perform the estimating, subcontractor and supplier solicitation, bid analysis, budgeting, scheduling, forecasting, and project-controls work. As the company expands, you will help develop the systems and processes required to scale the function, assist in building the team, and have the opportunity to develop into the leader of the estimating and project controls department. We are looking for someone who can do the work today, build better systems for tomorrow, and eventually lead others doing it. This is NOT primarily a quantity takeoff position. Takeoffs are part of the estimating process, but they represent only a small portion of this role. The primary responsibility is understanding complete project scope, developing and validating costs, obtaining real-world subcontractor and supplier pricing, establishing project budgets and schedules, and controlling those same costs and commitments throughout project execution. Core Responsibilities • Review plans, specifications, selections, and project information to understand and define complete project scope. • Develop detailed preliminary and construction estimates covering labor, materials, subcontractors, suppliers, equipment, and other project costs. • Develop clear scopes of work and identify missing scope, assumptions, allowances, inconsistencies, and cost risks. • Perform quantity takeoffs as necessary to support estimating. • Prepare and issue RFPs/RFQs to US subcontractors and suppliers. • Communicate directly with subcontractors and vendors to solicit pricing, obtain clarifications and revisions, and follow up on outstanding proposals. • Review and level subcontractor and supplier bids, including exclusions, qualifications, allowances, and scope discrepancies. • Validate estimates against current market pricing and historical project costs. • Convert approved estimates into structured project-control budgets. • Track estimated, bid, committed, actual, and forecast costs throughout construction. • Monitor budget variances, commitments, cost-to-complete, and forecast final project costs. • Track procurement, subcontract agreements, allowances, change orders, and major material purchases. • Develop and maintain project schedules and identify procurement, sequencing, and schedule risks. • Coordinate with project managers and field personnel to maintain accurate budgets, forecasts, and schedules. • Identify cost and schedule problems early and communicate them clearly to management. • Maintain organized estimating, procurement, cost-control, scheduling, and project reporting records. Systems Development & Company Growth We are building a company that can operate at substantially greater scale, and this person will have a meaningful role in developing the systems that support that growth. Responsibilities will include: • Develop and continuously improve company-wide estimating and project-control standards. • Build scalable estimating templates, cost databases, subcontractor bidding processes, budgeting systems, forecasting tools, and management reporting. • Standardize the transition from preconstruction estimating through procurement, construction, and closeout. • Create documented procedures that can be taught and delegated as the department grows. • Identify opportunities for automation and effective use of AI throughout estimating and project controls. • Help recruit, train, and supervise future estimating and project-controls personnel. • Ultimately have the opportunity to lead the estimating and project controls department as the company expands. Required Experience Substantial experience working on US-based construction projects is a firm requirement. Candidates without meaningful US construction estimating/project-controls experience will not be considered. We are looking for: • Minimum 9 years of relevant construction experience required. Preference will be given to candidates with 10–15+ years of experience and a demonstrated progression into senior estimating, project controls, systems development, and team leadership. • Significant direct experience estimating and/or controlling costs for US-based construction projects. • Strong experience with US residential construction, remodeling, additions, custom homes, or closely comparable building construction. • Demonstrated ability to develop complete project estimates, not simply produce quantity takeoffs. • Strong understanding of US construction methods, subcontractor scopes, labor and material pricing, terminology, procurement practices, and cost structures. • Experience preparing and issuing RFPs/RFQs to subcontractors and suppliers. • Experience reviewing, comparing, and leveling subcontractor proposals. • Experience establishing and tracking project budgets, commitments, actual costs, cost-to-complete, and forecast final costs. • Experience with construction scheduling and the relationship between schedule, procurement, and cost. • Advanced Excel skills. • Experience with construction software such as MS Project, or comparable platforms. • Excellent written and spoken English and the ability to communicate professionally and confidently with US subcontractors, suppliers, project managers, and company leadership. • Ability to work independently, exercise judgment, identify problems, and take ownership without constant supervision. Who This Role Is — and Is Not — For This role is suited to an experienced construction professional who can receive a set of plans and project information and independently determine: What needs to be included? What is missing? What will it actually cost? Who needs to provide pricing? What questions need to be answered? What needs to happen when? And once construction starts, are we actually performing against the plan? If your primary experience is producing quantity takeoffs from plans for someone else to estimate, this is not the right position. We are seeking someone capable of owning the broader preconstruction and project-controls process and who wants to take progressively greater responsibility as the company grows. Compensation & Growth Base compensation is expected to be $15–$22 USD/hour depending on experience and demonstrated capability. For an extraordinary candidate with exceptional US construction experience, judgment, systems-development ability, communication skills, and leadership potential, compensation may reach approximately $25 USD/hour. Exceptional performers may also have access to performance bonuses and profit-sharing opportunities as their contribution and responsibilities increase. This is intended to be a long-term position for someone who wants to grow with the company and ultimately has the capability to help build and lead a major business function. Must be able to work US-based central time zone hours. PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING This is a senior-level construction estimating and project controls position. It is not a virtual assistant, administrative support, takeoff-only, or trainee role. You must have substantial prior experience personally leading estimating and/or project controls for US-based construction projects. If you do not have this experience, please do not apply. We are not hiring someone to train into this function. HOW TO APPLY Please submit your resume together with a brief cover letter answering the questions below. 1. Approximately how many US-based construction and remodeling projects have you personally served as the lead estimator and/or primary project-controls professional on? Please state the approximate number, typical project values, project types, and the years during which you performed this work. 2. Describe one specific US-based residential construction or remodeling project for which you personally developed the estimate. What was the approximate construction value, what was your exact role, and what portions of the estimating process did you personally perform? 3. Describe one specific project where you personally solicited subcontractor or supplier proposals. What trade or material was being bid, approximately how many proposals did you obtain, and identify one scope difference, exclusion, or pricing discrepancy you found while comparing the proposals. 4. Describe one project where you continued working on cost control after the original estimate was completed. Give one specific example of a cost variance you identified during construction, including the original budget or estimate, what changed, and how you identified the issue. 5. Describe one estimating or project-controls system, spreadsheet, database, template, or workflow that you personally created or substantially improved. What problem was it intended to solve, what did you personally build or change, and how was it used afterward?

review_candidates.title: Postdoctoral Researcher in Soviet-African Educational Legacies and Alumni Networks
review_candidates.description: Are you interested in how Soviet education has shaped African professional lives, memories and contemporary international connections? Join our interdisciplinary research team to investigate the trajectories of Soviet-educated East Africans and the alumni organisations that reactivate these histories today. Working at the UvA Trace the afterlives of socialist internationalism During the Cold War, thousands of Africans studied at universities and other higher-education institutions in the Soviet Union and other socialist countries. Existing research tells us considerably more about their experiences abroad than about their lives after returning home. We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to study how Soviet-educated East Africans converted their acquired qualifications and connections into professional, political and social positions back home; how they remember and reinterpret their experiences; and how alumni organisations mobilise these histories today. You will join IRInA, an interdisciplinary ERC Starting Grant project examining how East African actors navigate a diversified landscape of international partnerships. You will collaborate with the principal investigator, a PhD researcher and another postdoctoral researcher while developing a clearly identifiable individual project. In your project, Uganda will be the principal case study, which can be potentially extended to include another East African country for a comparison. A good salary Your salary will be determined on the basis of your experience and seniority, in accordance with the Labour agreement. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Family matters Relocating to the Netherlands with your family? Find out about daycare, schooling, health insurance or employment options and support for your partner or spouse. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. All About This Vacancy This is what you will be doing Design and conduct an original postdoctoral project on Soviet-educated African professionals, memory and alumni networks, in consultation with the project leader; Undertake archival research, oral-history interviews and qualitative fieldwork in Uganda and potentially in other selected East African countries; Examine how former students and their families remember Soviet education, including professional formation, mobility, solidarity, friendship, racialisation and political change; Map and analyse alumni organisations and their relationships with other institutions, embassies, universities and educational or commercial intermediaries; Publish at least three peer-reviewed academic outputs, including at least two single- or lead-authored journal articles, and contribute to comparative project publications; Present findings at international conferences and contribute to project workshops, research communication, data management and team activities. This Is What We Ask Of You A completed PhD in history, anthropology, African studies, sociology, political science, international relations, or a related field; Experience with qualitative research, preferably including interviews, oral history, ethnographic fieldwork or archival research in (East) Africa; Knowledge of languages spoken in Uganda is a strong asset; knowledge of Russian or another language of the former Soviet Union is an advantage; Good command of written and spoken English and a publication record appropriate to your career stage; The ability to develop independent fieldwork design and willingness to undertake it in Uganda, while contributing actively to the larger project. This Is What We Offer You The employment will be for one year. Contingent on a positive performance evaluation the contract will be extended with two years. The preferred starting date is 1 February 2027; Depending on relevant experience, the salary at the start of the employment is between 3.706,- and 5.760,- gross per month based on full-time employment for a 38-hour working week. In addition, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% end-of-year allowance. The Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities is applicable; Excellent possibilities for further professional development and education; Funding and practical support for fieldwork, conference participation, research training and relevant archival visits within the project’s approved plans and budget; An inspiring academic and international work environment in the heart of Amsterdam. Your place at the UvA This is where you'll be working You will be part of IRInA, an interdisciplinary ERC Starting Grant project led by Dr. Gulnaz Sibgatullina and based at the University of Amsterdam. The research team combines historical, ethnographic and digital approaches. It includes the principal investigator, a PhD researcher and two postdoctoral researchers. In addition to your direct colleagues within the team, you will also join the vibrant community of researchers at ARTES (the Amsterdam School for Regional and Transnational Studies). The position is based in the department of History, European Studies and Religious Studies, capacity group European Studies (program group East European History supervised by Prof. Michael Kemper) in the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Amsterdam. About The Faculty Of Humanities From modern and classical languages, history, arts and culture, archaeology, religious studies and philosophy to new media, digital humanities, and conservation and restoration, the Faculty of Humanities encompasses a broad spectrum of innovative teaching and research. Based in the historic heart of Amsterdam, it maintains close ties with many partners in the cultural sector, society and the business community. In doing so, it forms part of a humanities hub of international standing. Important to know Your application & contact Questions? For questions about the position or department, you can contact us during office hours at: Gulnaz Sibgatullina, g.r.sibgatullina@uva.nl University Lecturer Application If you recognize yourself in the profile and are interested in the position, we look forward to receiving your application. Please send us your application, consisting of the documents listed below, in one single PDF file: A cover letter explaining your interest in the position and relevant experience;a curriculum vitae, including a list of publications; A research proposal of 1,500–2,000 words identifying the research questions, potential cases, methods, sources, relevant linguistic preparation, and a feasible three-year publication plan; One writing sample; The names and contact details of two academic referees. The vacancy closes on 15-10-2026. The first round of interviews will take place at the end of October 2026. Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion As an employer, the UvA maintains an equal opportunities policy. We value diversity and are fully committed to being a place where everyone feels at home. We nurture inquisitive minds and perseverance and allow room for persistent questioning. With us, curiosity and creativity are the prevailing culture. Studies show that women and members of underrepresented groups only apply for jobs if they meet 100% of the qualifications. Do you meet the educational requirements but not yet all of the requested experience? The UvA encourages you to apply anyway.

review_candidates.title: ONU Mujeres RO Americas & Caribbean, Especialista en género, ambiente y cambio climático, Home based, Consultoría Internacional
review_candidates.description: Background JOB DESCRIPTION I. Contexto organizacional La entidad de las Naciones Unidas para la Igualdad de Género y el Empoderamiento de las mujeres, ONU Mujeres, basándose en la visión de igualdad consagrada en la Carta de las Naciones Unidas, trabaja para eliminar la discriminación en contra de las mujeres y las niñas; por el empoderamiento de las mujeres, y para lograr la igualdad entre mujeres y hombres como socios y beneficiarios del desarrollo, por los derechos humanos, en las acciones humanitarias, en la paz y seguridad. Al colocar los derechos de las mujeres como el eje central de su labor, ONU Mujeres lidera y coordina los esfuerzos del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas para asegurar que los compromisos de igualdad y transversalidad de género se traduzcan en acciones en todo el mundo. Al mismo tiempo, ejerce un liderazgo sustantivo y coherente para apoyar las prioridades y los esfuerzos de los Estados Miembro, construyendo una asociación eficaz con el gobierno, la sociedad civil, así como con otros actores relevantes. ONU-Mujeres Aborda Integralmente Las Causas Profundas De La Desigualdad Desde Una Perspectiva De Transformación De Los Sistemas De Reproducción De Las Desigualdades De Género y Discriminaciones y Con Un Enfoque De Construcción De Paz En Torno a Voz, liderazgo y autonomías de las mujeres Fortalecimiento de marcos normativos multilaterales y regional, y leyes, políticas e instituciones que promuevan la igualdad de género a nivel nacional y subnacional; Participación efectiva y protección de las mujeres en todos los ámbitos de la construcción de la Paz, la Seguridad, y la acción humanitaria Acceso equitativo de las mujeres a los servicios, bienes y recursos; Financiamiento de la igualdad de género y el empoderamiento de las mujeres; Normas sociales positivas, incluida la participación de hombres y niños; Producción, análisis y utilización de estadísticas de género; y Coordinación del sistema de las Naciones Unidas para la igualdad de género y el empoderamiento de las mujeres. El Plan Estratégico 2026–2029 tiene como objetivo avanzar hacia la igualdad de género, el empoderamiento de todas las mujeres y las niñas y la realización plena de sus derechos humanos. El Plan está anclado en las obligaciones internacionales en materia de derechos humanos y en compromisos globales como la Convención sobre la Eliminación de Todas las Formas de Discriminación contra la Mujer (CEDAW), la Declaración y la Plataforma de Acción de Beijing, las resoluciones del Consejo de Seguridad de las Naciones Unidas sobre las mujeres, la paz y la seguridad, así como otros acuerdos intergubernamentales pertinentes, incluidas las resoluciones de la Asamblea General y las conclusiones convenidas de la Comisión de la Condición Jurídica y Social de la Mujer (CSW). Asimismo, contribuye directamente a la implementación de la Agenda 2030 para el Desarrollo Sostenible, los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible y el Pacto para el Futuro, situando la igualdad de género y el ODS 5 en el centro y en articulación con los demás objetivos. II. Antecedentes Desde inicios de 2023, el Hub Regional de Género, Ambiente y Cambio Climático de ONU Mujeres para América Latina y el Caribe ha trabajado estratégicamente para posicionar la igualdad de género y la participación efectiva de las mujeres en toda su diversidad en las agendas ambientales y climáticas de la región. Para ello, se diseñó e implementó una hoja de ruta regional que, articulando el mandato normativo de ONU Mujeres, la coordinación con el Sistema de Naciones Unidas y el apoyo técnico a los países, ha permitido consolidar el área como una plataforma regional estratégica para promover una acción climática y ambiental más justa, inclusiva y efectiva. En el ámbito normativo y de políticas públicas, el área ha apoyado la integración de la perspectiva de género en procesos nacionales y regionales vinculados a acción ambiental, justicia climática y derechos de acceso; así como en posiciones regionales para las negociaciones internacionales. Entre los principales avances se encuentran el fortalecimiento de la transversalización de género en el marco del Acuerdo de Escazú, mediante la adopción de la Decisión III/4 y guías de transversalización de la perspectiva de género; el apoyo a la participación y posicionamiento de mujeres indígenas en procesos de la Convención sobre la Diversidad Biológica; y el acompañamiento, junto con otras agencias y en alianza con los Puntos Focales Nacionales de Género y Cambio Climático, de la participación de ALC en las negociaciones de la Convención Marco de las Naciones Unidas sobre el Cambio Climático (CMNUCC). Este trabajo contribuyó a la extensión por diez años del Plan de Trabajo de Lima y a la adopción del Plan de Acción de Género de Belem en la COP30. En materia de fortalecimiento institucional, capacidades y generación de evidencia, ONU Mujeres desarrolló un conjunto de 21 indicadores de género y cambio climático orientados a informar la toma de decisiones públicas y lideró, junto con CEPAL y PNUMA, la creación de un Grupo de Trabajo Regional sobre estadísticas de género y clima en el marco de la Conferencia Regional sobre Estadísticas, contribuyendo a avanzar hacia metodologías más armonizadas y datos comparables entre países. Asimismo, se han desarrollado herramientas, metodologías, manuales de transversalización e género en las políticas climáticas, procesos de formación nacional y subnacional e intercambios de conocimiento Sur-Sur para fortalecer las capacidades de instituciones nacionales y subnacionales. El área también ha fortalecido la participación y liderazgo de organizaciones de mujeres y feministas, con especial atención a mujeres indígenas, rurales, afrodescendientes y defensoras de derechos humanos ambientales. A través de apoyos técnicos, pequeñas subvenciones y espacios regionales de fortalecimiento y articulación; contribuyendo al fortalecimiento de sus capacidades para participar en procesos de gobernanza ambiental y climática e incidencia en espacios de decisión nacionales, regionales y globales. Finalmente, se ha consolidado una base regional de conocimiento y visibilidad mediante campañas públicas, publicaciones, metodologías, materiales audiovisuales y un repositorio regional que facilita el acceso y sostenibilidad de los conocimientos generados. Estos esfuerzos se complementan con un espacio web especializado del Hub Regional sobre Género, Ambiente y Justicia Climática, fortaleciendo el posicionamiento y alcance del trabajo de ONU Mujeres en la región. Sobre esta base, la siguiente etapa requiere consolidar la sostenibilidad de los resultados alcanzados, escalar su impacto y profundizar las alianzas estratégicas, avanzando de manera progresiva del apoyo a los países para la adopción de compromisos hacia el acompañamiento de su implementación efectiva. Para ello, se identifica la necesidad de contar con un/a Especialista Regional en Género, Ambiente y Cambio Climático que impulse la implementación de la estrategia regional y la hoja de ruta elaborado con apoyo del proyecto, fortalezca las alianzas regionales y contribuya a asegurar la sostenibilidad, escalabilidad e impacto del trabajo de ONU Mujeres en materia de igualdad de género, acción ambiental y justicia climática en ALC La persona contratada desempeñará sus funciones con un alto grado de independencia y autonomía para la toma de decisiones en el ámbito de su asignación. II. Objetivo Contribuir al fortalecimiento, posicionamiento y escalamiento de la agenda regional de género, ambiente y cambio climático de ONU Mujeres en América Latina y el Caribe, mediante la implementación efectiva de iniciativas programáticas, el desarrollo de alianzas estratégicas, la generación de conocimiento e incidencia, y el fortalecimiento de mecanismos de cooperación que promuevan la integración de la igualdad de género en las políticas y acciones ambientales y climáticas, y de las dimensiones ambientales y climáticas en la agenda de igualdad de género. Objetivos específicos Asegurar la implementación exitosa de la primera fase del programa regional “Género, ambiente y cambio climático: potenciando acciones eficientes, justas y efectivas”. Contribuir al posicionamiento y fortalecimiento de la agenda regional de género, ambiente y cambio climático mediante asistencia técnica, generación de alianzas estratégicas, participación en espacios regionales y multilaterales, y apoyo al relacionamiento con actores clave de los sectores ambiental y climático. Impulsar la sostenibilidad y escalamiento de la agenda regional de género, ambiente y cambio climático, fortaleciendo mecanismos de cooperación, alianzas Sur-Sur y la preparación técnica y programática de una posible segunda fase del proyecto. Apoyar el desarrollo y la visibilidad de la agenda regional de género, ambiente y cambio climático de ONU Mujeres, incluyendo acciones de comunicación e incidencia para promover la integración de la perspectiva de género en las políticas ambientales y climáticas, y de los temas ambientales y climáticos en la agenda de igualdad de género. IV. Alcance de los objetivos/responsabilidades Se espera que el/la titular lleve a cabo las responsabilidades y actividades descritas a continuación con la finalidad del logro del el/los objetivo/s de la consultoría. Dichas Responsabilidades Incluirán Asegurar la implementación técnica y el seguimiento del programa regional “Género, ambiente y cambio climático: potenciando acciones eficientes, justas y efectivas”, mediante la elaboración y presentación de informes de avance que documenten el cumplimiento de resultados, productos e indicadores. Generar propuestas para dar continuidad y garantizar la sostenibilidad de los resultados del programa regional, incluyendo marco de resultados, teoría de cambio, principales líneas estratégicas, actividades prioritarias, indicadores, presupuesto preliminar y realizar el seguimiento técnico de las consultas y observaciones del donante. Proporcionar asistencia técnica a las Oficinas País para impulsar la implementación de la estrategia regional desarrollada en el marco del proyecto, así como para fortalecer iniciativas y alianzas estratégicas que contribuyan al logro de sus objetivos y resultados. Desarrollar productos de comunicación y posicionamiento de los resultados e impactos del proyecto regional. V. review_candidates.title: Executive | Stakeholder Management & CDSU
review_candidates.description: JOB SUMMARY Support the planning, development, implementation and governance of Stakeholder Engagement and Community Development & Social Upliftment (CDSU) initiatives to strengthen stakeholder relationships and deliver sustainable social impact. The role is responsible for programme development and management, stakeholder engagement, monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL), governance, budgeting, audit coordination and reporting, while contributing to cross-functional initiatives that advance EPF's strategic objectives. JOB RESPONSIBILITIES Design, develop and recommend CDSU programmes and initiatives aligned with EPF's strategic objectives, informed by emerging social issues, stakeholder expectations and national priorities. Support the planning, implementation and review of CDSU programmes from inception to completion, ensuring delivery within approved scope, timeline and budget. Conduct needs assessments, research and benchmarking to inform programme development and continuous improvement. Support the development of CDSU strategies, annual workplans and programme roadmaps. Develop concept papers, programme proposals, Board papers, management papers and other approval documents in compliance with EPF's governance, procurement and approval frameworks. Implement Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) frameworks by establishing programme KPIs, outcome indicators and impact measurement methodologies to assess programme performance and drive continuous improvement. Support engagement with government agencies, NGOs, academic institutions, social enterprises and strategic partners to strengthen collaboration and programme delivery. Coordinate stakeholder consultations, manage strategic partnerships and collaborative initiatives, and incorporate stakeholder feedback to enhance programme design and implementation. Prepare reports, dashboards, presentation materials, executive summaries and other management updates for the Board, Management and external stakeholders, as required. Support the planning and management of the Unit's annual operating budget by monitoring programme expenditure, optimising budget utilisation and ensuring the prudent and efficient use of resources. Support internal and external audit exercises by preparing documentation, coordinating information requests and facilitating the timely resolution of audit findings. Collaborate with other units and sections within the Department to support cross-functional initiatives, special projects and organisational priorities, providing strategic and operational expertise where required. SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS Malaysian citizen Passed the Malay Language (including oral test) at Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) level. Bachelor Degree (Honours) recognised by the Government from any local or abroad higher learning institution or qualification. Minimum 4 - 6 years of experience in the IT field, including experience in a supervisory or leadership position. Relevant working experience in community development, corporate social responsibility (CSR), sustainability, social impact, stakeholder engagement or programme management. Demonstrated experience in working directly with communities, including conducting needs assessments, engaging beneficiaries and community partners, and designing or implementing community-based programmes. Ability to engage respectfully with diverse communities and stakeholders, understand their needs, and translate insights into practical, sustainable programmes that deliver measurable social impact. A strategic thinker with good communication and interpersonal skills. Highly organised and perform well under pressure. Strong research and analytical skills. Problem solving skills with incredible attention to detail PLACEMENT Stakeholder Management & CDSU, Strategic Communications & Stakeholder Management, Corporate Affairs Department JOB STATUS Permanent All applications are strictly CONFIDENTIAL and only shortlisted candidates will be called in for interview. Applications are deemed UNSUCCESSFUL if there is no feedback from the EPF 2 MONTHS after the closing date of advertisement.
